title: Intro: Redwood x HelixCloud - SaaS GPU Orchestration Partnership
summary: Introductory discovery between Redwood AE/SE and HelixCloud partnership and platform leads. Covered partner model (reseller vs tech integration), orchestration for multi-tenant SaaS GPU pools, SSO/KMS requirements for private deployments, basic latency/cost tradeoffs and benchmarking plan. Agreed to run a small two-week pilot: integration checklist, partner contract intro, and shared benchmark spreadsheet.
topics: partner models: reseller vs embedded SaaS
action_items: Samir - send partner one-pager + pricing rubric (due 2025-10-03)
Jules - share benchmark template and SLO checklist (due 2025-10-06)
Priya - provide HelixCloud infra diagram and expected workload profile (due 2025-10-08)
Erin - intro legal to Redwood partnerships team (due 2025-10-07)
next_steps: Schedule technical deep dive for capacity routing and autoscaling (SE-led)
Agree pilot scope and sign MOU to kick off two-week integration pilot
Exchange security docs (SOC2 report, data flow diagram, KMS options)
Populate benchmark sheet with sample workloads
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-30
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Moreno (Redwood SE), Erin Tan (HelixCloud Head of Partnerships), Diego Marquez (Platform Lead), Priya Shah (Cloud Architect)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. This is Samir from Redwood Inference, I'm an AE on the partnerships team. With me is Jules, our solutions engineer. You good to start Erin?
[00:12] Erin: Yeah for sure, thanks Samir. We wanted to kick off a quick intro — HelixCloud is looking to expand our marketplace with a SaaS GPU orchestration offering and thought Redwood might be a fit to either resell or embed your runtime for inference.
[00:27] Samir: Awesome, yeah super excited. Quick context from our side — Redwood is focused on inference serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, tooling for cost optimization and observability. Jules will cover some of the technical fit.
[00:40] Jules: Hey all, hi. Quick note, I'll try not to nerd out too much up front, but we want to understand Helix's model — are you looking to be a reseller, or do you want to integrate Redwood as an onram— like embed our runtime behind your control plane?
[00:56] Diego: Good question. The ask from leadership is twofold: one, a managed marketplace where customers can consume models via Helix UI and we provision GPU capacity; two, an option to offer a private deployment for regulated customers where Helix still manages access but customers have a VPC. So either reseller or deep integration could work.
[01:18] Priya: From infra perspective, we run multi-tenant Kubernetes clusters across three regions, NVLink-backed A100 and some Ampere M40 fleets. We have a central control plane that assigns workloads and does autoscaling. Key constraint: we need per-tenant isolation and KMS integration for customer keys.
[01:38] Jules: Got it. A few quick things that matter for Redwood side: 1) how you want routing and tenancy to work — do you want us to expose a hosted API you call, or do you want to bring Redwood Private to your VPC? 2) latency SLOs — what do customers expect for tail latency? 3) billing integration — will Helix handle billing and resell or do you want to pass usage through Redwood?
[02:00] Erin: On SLOs, most customers expect sub-250ms for typical chat completions but we have long-tail customers who accept higher for batch. Billing ideally goes through Helix — we want a per-tenant usage meter so we can bill them.
[02:15] Samir: That maps well to two common patterns we've seen: hosted API + reseller billing, or private deployment where you run our control plane and we provide a partner license. Hosted is fastest to market; private gives more control for KMS/VPC.
[02:29] Diego: For the hosted path, are there concerns about data residency? Some of our EU customers require their data to stay in EU regions and SOC2 attestation.
[02:40] Jules: We support region pinning and have SOC2 and ISO attestation docs we can share. For EU-only flows we recommend routing to our EU-hosted clusters or deploying Private in your region.
[02:52] Priya: KMS — do you support external key stores? We use HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS depending on customer.
[03:01] Samir: Yes, Redwood integrates with external KMS/HSMs for key management. There may be some connector work for Vault but that's common.
[03:09] Erin: Cool. Diego, any red flags on the capacity side?
[03:13] Diego: Two things: multi-tenant GPU orchestration and burst capacity. We don't want noisy neighbors. Also need predictable throughput for priority customers. How do you handle isolation at the runtime level?
[03:24] Jules: Good Q. Our serving runtime supports dedicated GPU pools and tenant-aware routing. You can pin workloads to dedicated pools or use soft quotas with priority lanes. We also do KV/prefix caching to reduce per-token compute for repeated prompts — that helps cost. Realistically for noisy neighbors, recommended pattern is mixture of dedicated and shared pools with strict scheduling.
[03:42] Samir: And we provide observability for token-level latency and cost so you can pass that into your billing engine.
[03:48] Erin: On the integration model, does Redwood support a partner SDK or a control-plane API we can call from Helix?
[03:56] Jules: Yes, there's a REST SDK and a control-plane API for model routing, rollout, and quota management. There are also webhooks for events. For deep embedding we'd do an SE-led integration to map your capacity APIs to our routing policies.
[04:11] Diego: Excellent. On benchmarking — we'd like to run a representative set: chat completions, embedding loads, and some long-sequence generation. Any suggestions on sequence lengths and batch sizes we should test?
[04:24] Jules: Typical: chat completions (context ~1k tokens), embeddings (512 tokens), and a few long prompts up to 8k tokens for customer X. Batching will depend on latency SLOs; we'll propose a sheet with recommended batch sizes and quantization options.
[04:39] [crosstalk] Priya: Sorry Jules, when you say quantization options do you mean 8-bit/4-bit? We do worry about quality.
[04:45] Jules: Yep, 8-bit/4-bit quant is supported for many open models; we'll flag expected quality regressions and give recommended model variants. For production-critical customers we recommend lower quant or dedicated pools.
[04:58] Erin: Can you talk about fallback policies? If our primary region is saturated, can Redwood route to another region or a lower-cost model?
[05:07] Samir: Yes, we have smart routing policies that can fallback by latency or cost — you can set preferences to prioritize region or to allow cross-region fallback. For enterprise we can also set model variants as fallbacks to preserve availability.
[05:21] Diego: Great. On billing integration — we want token-level metering data exported to our billing system hourly. Is that available?
[05:29] Jules: We emit usage events and can provide per-tenant token counts with timestamps. For reseller billing we can set up a usage feed. There's format work but it's standard.
[05:38] Priya: About security reviews — legal will want to see SOC2 and penetration testing reports, plus an architecture diagram showing data flow.
[05:47] Samir: We can share SOC2 and have a standard security questionnaire we fill out. We'll also provide a samples of audit logs and activity traces.
[05:56] Erin: Awesome. From partnership GTM side — Helix would likely want to list Redwood as a preferred inference runtime in our marketplace and we may co-sell. Any partner program high-level terms?
[06:06] Samir: We have a partner one-pager and reseller program — margins depend on committed volume. I'll send that over. We also offer joint marketing assets for launch.
[06:15] Diego: On timeline, if we did a pilot, how long to stand up?
[06:20] Jules: For hosted API flow it's a matter of wiring up auth and routing — we can run a pilot in 1-2 weeks. For deep private integration into Helix VPCs, estimate 3-6 weeks depending on KMS and networking.
[06:33] Priya: Network-wise we use VPC peering and private link between regions. Any special ports or firewall rules required?
[06:41] Jules: We usually request a couple of egress endpoints and cert-based mutual TLS for control plane. We'll provide a network checklist.
[06:50] [00:07:05] Samir: ok, I want to make sure we capture the commercial ask — Erin, you said Helix wants to bill customers directly and operate the marketplace. So the initial pilot could be hosted-resell to speed to market and then expand to a Private integration for regulated tenants. Does that sound right?
[07:05] Erin: Yes that's our preferred unfolding. Quick pilot to prove customer experience and metrics, then commit to Private for top-tier customers.
[07:13] Diego: For the pilot, what's success criteria? Latency under X, cost per 1k tokens under Y, and no data leakage — basically measurable SLOs.
[07:23] Jules: We'll propose a simple SLO set: p95 latency under 300ms for chat (1k tokens), embedding throughput of N qps, and accuracy/regression thresholds for model outputs.
[07:34] Priya: Also need to confirm that audit logs include per-call metadata and that KV cache entries aren't shared across tenants.
[07:42] Samir: That's fundamental — tenant isolation is default for KV cache when using dedicated pools; when shared we namespace entries. We'll outline details in the security questionnaire.
[07:54] Erin: Anything on revenue share? We expect a margin for Helix for marketplace sellers.
[07:59] Samir: We'll include a high-level rebate schedule in the partner one-pager; precise terms come after MOU.
[08:07] [00:09:00] Diego: A few technical nitty-gritty: do you have GPU affinity settings, bin-packing, and pre-warm instances for burst to reduce cold-start latency?
[08:18] Jules: Yes, affinity/pinning and pre-warm pools are supported. We also can do model sharding for very large models. Cold start reductions are possible with pre-warmed workers and KV cache priming.
[08:29] Priya: Wondering about orchestrator — do you integrate with K8s directly or do you require a specific runtime?
[08:36] Jules: We run in Kubernetes but abstract the runtime. For Private we provide operators and CRDs to manage the runtime and GPU pools. For hosted you simply hit the API.
[08:47] Erin: Ok, this is great. Can we talk about the pilot scope quickly and agree owners?
[08:52] Samir: Sure. Proposed pilot: 2 weeks, hosted-resell path, run three benchmarks (chat, embeddings, long-gen), measure latency and cost, validate billing feed and basic SSO. Owners: Redwood SE (Jules) runs benchmark script and provides template; Helix infra (Priya/Diego) provide sample workloads and test accounts; Helix Partnerships (Erin) coordinate customers and legal intro.
[09:12] Priya: That works. We'll provide workload profile and infra diagram by next week.
[09:18] Jules: We'll deliver benchmark sheet and a small test harness — will need an API key and sample model config.
[09:24] Diego: On API key, for security we'd prefer token scoped to pilot and short TTL.
[09:30] Samir: No problem — one-time pilot key with limited scope.
[09:33] [00:12:00] Erin: Any other blockers we're forgetting?
[09:36] Diego: Legal and procurement will want a basic MOU.
[09:39] Samir: We'll draft a short MOU and send. Erin, you'll intro the legal contact per action item?
[09:44] Erin: Yep, I'll intro.
[09:46] Jules: On the technical deep dive — I propose we schedule a 60-minute call next week to go through capacity routing and autoscaling policies. We'll demo how to pin tenants and configure fallback policies.
[09:58] Priya: Works for me, mornings PT are best.
[10:01] Samir: Great. Any competitive concerns? Diego: We have some customers already testing MegaCloud AI and EdgeServe. They both struggle on cost; MegaCloud's latency is good but expensive.
[10:14] Jules: Good to know. We'll highlight our cost-control features in the follow-up.
[10:19] Erin: Ok let's recap real quick.
[10:21] Samir: Recap — Redwood to send partner one-pager and pricing rubric, Jules to share benchmark template and network checklist, Helix (Priya/Diego) to send infra diagram and workload profile, Erin to intro legal. Then schedule a technical deep dive.
[10:36] Priya: Timeline? We'll aim to have infra diagram and workload profile by 2025-10-08.
[10:43] Samir: We'll target the SE deep dive week of 2025-10-06. Pilot scoped to start mid-October if MOU signed.
[10:51] Erin: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[10:54] Samir: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hearings, some speaker labels simplified.
